summary: Rotational embed shift after quantized rollout causing rerank latency spike and quality drift
description: Issue summary: BrightDocs reports intermittent rerank endpoint slowdowns and worse top-k ordering after a scheduled rollout of a quantized embedding variant. Impact: Production rerank latency increased from ~60ms median to 300–700ms for a subset of multilingual requests, and top-k quality degraded (different top1 in ~4% of queries). Environment: prod:us-west (BrightDocs customer, enterprise tier) using redwood-embed-large-v2 for embed generation and rerank-mono-1.3 for reranking. Timeframe: regression began ~2026-02-19 23:40 UTC immediately following a background rollout of embed-quantized-v2. Observed behavior: - Increased tail latency and occasional 504 timeouts from reranker service. - Rerank output ordering changes for multilingual inputs (notably Japanese and German) compared to pre-rollout baseline. - Errors are correlated with larger batch sizes and higher tokenization variance. Expected behavior: Stable latency distributions and consistent rerank ordering compared to baseline model/quantization profile.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Use BrightDocs test tenant with multilingual prompt set (EN/JA/DE). 2) Send embedding requests to the hosted embeddings API pinned to embed-quantized-v2 (as rolled out). 3) Immediately call /rerank endpoint with embeddings returned. 4) Repeat with batch sizes 1, 8, 32 and observe latency and top-k. 5) Repeat same input pinned to redwood-embed-large-v2 (non-quant) and compare ordering and timing. Expected: non-quant path shows baseline latency and stable top-k; quantized path shows latency spikes and top-k deviations in failing cases.

investigation_notes: Initial hypothesis: quantized embedding variant introduced a rotational/packing alignment change for the vector layout (byte/word ordering) that interacts with reranker's batched distance computation, causing KV merge path to reserialize and fall back to slow path. Evidence: - Correlation between rollout window and spike in KV-cache-mismatch logs. - Failing cases show embeddings with expected dimension 768 but with anomalous low-entropy in trailing 64 dims for some languages. - When reranker receives embeddings with minor orientation shift, internal SIMD kernels choose fallback numeric path with per-item deserialization, doubling latency. Tests run: 1) Replayed failing requests against non-quant embed service -> baseline latency and ordering restored. 2) Manually re-encoded quant vectors with an extra byte-order normalization step before rerank -> latency restored but quality still slightly off. 3) Injected small perturbation (sign flip) into a copy of embeddings and observed similar ordering changes, indicating sensitivity to orientation in multilingual subspaces. Additional logs: linked internal trace: trace-id 7f3b2a67 (SRE)
resolution: Mitigation: Rolled back embed-quantized-v2 rollout for BrightDocs and any tenants still on auto-bump; reverted to redwood-embed-large-v2 for affected customers at 2026-02-20 02:10 UTC which restored baseline latency and ordering. Hotfix: Added input-vector schema checksum and dimensionality/orientation assertion in embeddings-service to detect nonconformant serialization and reject or normalize before proxying to reranker (hotfix PR merged: https://github.com/redwood-inference/embeddings-service/pull/1987). Permanent fix plan: 1) Add unit/regression tests that exercise multilingual tokenization variance against quantized transforms. 2) Update reranker to tolerate minor orientation differences by inserting a fast normalization kernel and fallback thresholds. 3) Add rollout gating metrics (KV-cache-mismatch rate, tail latency delta by language) to the deployment pipeline.
